name: Cowpea Rust
description: A fungal rust disease that produces brown pustules on cowpea leaves, stems, and pods. It is favored by moderate temperatures and high humidity, causing defoliation and significant yield reduction.
symptoms: Small brown or reddish-brown pustules on lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupturing to release powdery rust spores
Yellow halos surrounding pustules on upper leaf surfaces
Leaves turning yellow and dropping prematurely
Pod infection causing reduced seed quality
causes: Survival on crop debris between seasons
treatments: Apply fungicides containing tebuconazole or propiconazole
Spray mancozeb at 7-10 day intervals during humid periods
Use sulfur-based fungicides as preventive treatment
Remove severely infected leaves when practical
prevention: Maintain adequate plant spacing for ventilation
Remove and destroy crop residue after harvest
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening
